sections.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability
sections.content: Briefly define Conditional Probability P(A|B) as focusing on a reduced sample space. Use a Venn diagram to visually show the 'slice' of A inside B.
sections.example: Visualizing a grid of 100 people; highlighting only those who own a dog (B) and then identifying the subset who also own a cat (A).

sections.title: The Concept of Independence
sections.content: Explain that events A and B are independent if P(A|B) = P(A). Visually demonstrate this as 'the presence of B does not change the ratio of A in the universe'.
sections.example: Flipping a coin twice: The result of the first flip does not change the 50/50 probability distribution of the second flip.

sections.title: Introducing Bayes' Theorem
sections.content: Introduce the theorem as a mechanism to update beliefs (Posterior) based on new evidence (Likelihood). Use a 'Probability Tree' animation showing the flow from Prior to Posterior.
sections.example: A 'Medical Detective' scenario: Given a positive test result (Evidence), what is the actual probability of having the disease (Posterior)?

sections.title: Integration: When Bayes Meets Independence
sections.content: Show how independence simplifies the Likelihood calculation within Bayes' Theorem. Explain that when events are independent, the math simplifies from complex joint distributions to simple products.
sections.example: A robot sensor: If sensors A and B are independent, the probability of both detecting an obstacle is simply P(A) * P(B), making the Bayesian update much faster.

sections.title: Summary & Application Loop
sections.content: Summarize the core takeaway: Independence simplifies computation, while Bayes' Theorem provides the logic for learning from data.
sections.example: Applying the framework to an email spam filter: Independent keywords (words appearing independently) are used in a Bayesian classifier to label an email as 'Spam' or 'Ham'.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite Warm-up: Conditional Probability
lecture_lines: Conditional probability focuses on a reduced sample space.
Think of it as zooming into event B.
We only count outcomes where both A and B happen.
animations: Fade in rectangle representing full sample space #FFFFFF.
Highlight subset B (dog owners) with color #FF9900.
Highlight overlapping subset A (cat owners) with color #00CCFF.
Zoom in on the intersection A and B.
Final label showing P(A|B) as the ratio of intersection.

storyboard.title: The Concept of Independence
lecture_lines: Independence means knowing B gives no info on A.
The probability of A remains unchanged by B.
Visually, the ratio of A is constant throughout.
animations: Animate ratio of A remaining constant despite change in B.

storyboard.title: Introducing Bayes' Theorem
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem updates beliefs with new evidence.
Think like a sniffer dog seeking truth.
Adjust it based on new likelihood data.
Arrive at a refined posterior probability.
animations: Display Prior probability tree with branches #FFCC00.
Animate flow from Prior to Posterior using Bayes formula #FFFFFF.
Show final state: updated belief based on Evidence.

storyboard.title: Integration: When Bayes Meets Independence
lecture_lines: Independence makes Bayesian calculations much simpler.
Joint probabilities become simple products of individual terms.
This acceleration is vital for real-time systems.
animations: Display complex joint probability formula in #FFFFFF.
Show final product P(A) * P(B) in #00FF00.

storyboard.title: Summary & Application Loop
lecture_lines: Bayes' Theorem provides the logic for learning.
Together, they power modern data classifiers.
animations: Show loop icon connecting Independence to Bayes #FFCC00.
Animate email filter nodes with color #00CCFF.
